- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward by 2–4% per day of sentiment decay.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period prices (days 20–30); apply a 3–5% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or bearish in last 5 days.
